text_blocks.snippet: Opsumit (macitentan) can cause several common and serious side effects. It is prescribed to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

list.snippet: Nasopharyngitis or common cold / stuffy nose (up to 20%)
Bronchitis or upper respiratory tract infections (11% to 15%)
Anemia (low red blood cell count, around 13%)

Serious Birth Defects / Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Opsumit can cause severe harm or death to an unborn fetus. Women who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting treatment and use reliable, dual contraception during therapy and for one month after stopping.

Liver Damage / Hepatotoxicity: Opsumit can affect liver function. Doctors check liver enzymes before starting treatment. Seek immediate medical care for signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe upper right stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting.
Fluid Retention and Swelling: Peripheral edema (swelling of the hands, legs, or feet) or fluid buildup can occur, usually during the first few weeks of treatment.
Decreased Red Blood Cells (Anemia): Significant drops in hemoglobin can happen early in treatment and may occasionally require a blood transfusion.
Decreased Sperm Count: Opsumit may reduce sperm counts and impact male fertility.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more detailed safety guidelines through the Official Opsumit Website or check the full medication outline via GoodRx Opsumit Side Effects Guide. Side effects can also be reported to the FDA MedWatch Program.
If you or someone you care for is taking Opsumit, let me know:

list.snippet: Are you experiencing a specific side effect (such as swelling, fatigue, or headaches)?
